newsitem.title: UK: May Forties programme set lower at 22.45 mln bbls.
newsitem.headline: May Forties programme set lower at 22.45 mln bbls.

text.p: May's UK North Sea Forties programme schedules liftings totalling 22.45 million barrels, down from a revised 23.3 million in April, traders said on Wednesday.

The difference, 850,000 barrels, is the equivalent of 1.7 standard 500,000-barrel cargoes less than the revised April programme but is 4.15 million barrels, or eight cargoes below the original April schedule.
The May programme is made up of 38 cargoes ranging from 400,000 to 700,000 barrels with a further 1.55 million barrels which will go direct to Forties pipeline operator BP's refinery at Grangemouth.

April's Forties programme originally scheduled 44 cargoes but six cargoes, totalling 3.3 million barrels, have since been cancelled because of lower than expected production from fields contributing into the blend.
May being a day longer than April, daily liftings of Forties should run at 724,000 bpd compared to 777,000 bpd for the revised April programme and 887,000 bpd for the orginal April schedule.
Maintenance is planned at BP's Forties A, C and E platforms in the last week of May and at Marathon's Brae A and B platforms starting in the last week of May.
Forties loads at BP's Hound Point terminal in eastern Scotland.
